title: Contractable throughput terms, notice windows, and degradation rules
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Produce a concise, contract-ready definition set for 'assured throughput' in Dedicated plans, plus an operational remediation and notice lifecycle. Deliverables: 1) Metric definitions for billed vs. guaranteed capacity (tokens/minute, sustained window, burst envelope); 2) Error-budget math and credit computation templates customers can consume; 3) Standard contract clauses (notice, measurement windows, exclusions, autoscale interlock, failover); 4) Runbook for SB/CS teams to calculate credits and close incidents; 5) Example customer-facing notification templates and escalation ladder.

Measurement model: We propose measuring assured throughput as "committed tokens per minute (CTPM)" observed at the edge routing layer and reconciled to model variants by quantized equivalence factors. Primary SLA metric: 99th percentile of per-minute CTPM measured over a rolling 30-day window, with outage windows calculated in 1-minute buckets. Degradation bands: Full (>= 95% of CTPM), Partial (80-95%), Significant (<80%). Burst allowance: customers are guaranteed sustained CTPM for 95% of 10-minute windows in a 30-day period, with a configurable burst credit pool that can be consumed for short spikes.

Error budget and credits: Error budget = committed_tokens_per_month - measured_served_tokens_month. When error budget is breached for >2 consecutive billing days, credits are computed proportional to shortfall: credit = min(10% of monthly fee, shortfall_ratio * monthly_fee * remediation_multiplier). The remediation_multiplier is 1 for first two breaches, 1.5 thereafter in 90-day rolling horizon. Credits are issued after verification and root-cause review, typically within billing cycle + 30 days.

Notice, measurement windows and exclusions: Customer must provide a 24-hour notice for planned maintenance that might affect throughput; Redwood will provide a 72-hour notice for any planned changes that will materially affect committed capacity. Exclusions include force majeure, customer misconfiguration (network misrouting, excessive concurrency misaligned with reserved buckets), and scheduled maintenance explicitly accepted via the console. Measurement windows exclude identified customer-side networking incidents where TCP-level losses exceed 1% and a traceroute from customer to Redwood edge indicates transit path errors.

Autoscale interlock and failover: Dedicated autoscaling may be enabled as an optional contract add-on. When enabled, the autoscaler will attempt transparent capacity lift for sudden demand spikes up to burst allowance. If autoscale is not available, the contract degrades according to the degradation bands above and credits apply. The autoscale interlock clause ties crediting to observed failure of autoscaler to provision capacity within defined ramp windows (e.g., 10 minutes to allocate an additional reserved shard).

Acceptance criteria: 1) Legal-approved clause language for SLA and credits; 2) Implementation doc mapping telemetry signals (edge rps, token counts, quantized model weights) to contractual metric; 3) One-pager runbook for support + finance to compute credits; 4) Sample email templates for customer notice and credit reconciliation; 5) Tests in staging that simulate capacity degradation and produce expected credit calculations.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: specific per-customer negotiated adjustments to the credit multiplier (handled by Sales ops) and KMS/HSM regulated attestations (handled in separate Private contract initiative).
comments: 2025-02-15 - Aisha Patel: Initial draft and problem statement added. Linked to PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated/throughput-contracts (internal). Requested legal review after initial metrics draft.
2025-02-18 - Legal (Joan Kline): Reviewed high-level credit formula; asked for explicit cap language and sample calculation. Action: product to add worked example with numbers.

2025-02-20 - Marco Rivera: Engineering feasibility check: mapping 'committed tokens' to model-variant equivalents requires a quantization table per model family. Eng to produce mapping by 2025-03-03 (ENG-19102 assigned).

2025-02-25 - Support (Diego Huang): Noted operational concern: customers will frequently dispute burst accounting. Proposed adding per-customer burst ledger export via the Console. Action: PM to add console export requirement.

2025-03-01 - Finance (Priya Nair): Agreed with proportional credit proposal but requested that credits auto-apply only after post-incident RCA is completed to avoid erroneous payouts. We should include a 'provisional credit' flag in billing exports.
2025-03-03 - Marco Rivera: Added note in measurement model: use edge-level sampling invariant to include model-variant multipliers. ENG-19102 has started instrumenting metrics.
activity: Decision: Use 99th percentile over 30-day rolling window for SLA binding metric.
Trade-off: 30-day window smooths transient noise but may delay remediation — mitigated by short-term incident thresholds and provisional credits.
Open question: How to treat synthetic traffic used in customer tests? Proposal: exclude authenticated test tokens if customer registers test ranges in advance.
Next steps: 1) Produce worked credit example; 2) Legal to draft final clause; 3) Engineering to expose a burst ledger API; 4) Console to add 'SLA exports' toggle for customers.
work_notes: Worked example (to be included in next revision): Customer A: committed 1,000,000 tokens/day (CTPM average ~694 tokens/min). Measured served tokens in month = 27,000,000 vs committed 30,000,000 => shortfall_ratio = 0.10. If monthly fee = $50k, credit = min(10%*$50k, 0.10*$50k*1) = min($5k, $5k) => $5k credit.
customer_templates:
Customer notification (72h planned change): 
Subject: Redwood: Upcoming change that affects Dedicated capacity (Customer action required)
Body: We will be performing a change to capacity allocation on <date>. Expected impact: <summary>. If you have a reserved capacity commitment, please expect an adjusted availability during the maintenance window. Contact support@redwood.ai if you need a maintenance exception.

Incident credit notification: 
Subject: Redwood: Throughput credit applied for incident on <date>
Body: After investigation we determined a shortfall of X% against your committed throughput. We have applied a credit of $Y to invoice Z. Details and RCA: <link>
